correctness.rationale: For a simply connected convex Euclidean strip, every based nontrivial loop lifts from a point to its image under a nonidentity glide power; the straight segment realizes minimal length. Even powers minimize at 4L² and odd powers at L²+4y². Uniform area yields Q uniform on [0,H/(sqrt3 L)], hence X=min(1,Q²). Piecewise moments follow by exact integration. The exact nonnegative factorization (9r-10)²(27r²+60r+100)/(7500r⁴) establishes the universal normalized bound 729/2500 and unique equality at r=10/9. The independent checker confirms exact rational cases and identity, not replacing this general proof.

value.rationale: Pointwise essential-loop length is a natural local metric-topological invariant. Its full area distribution changes structure when a twice-winding loop overtakes a primitive loop, and the unique sharp area-normalized squared-length variance maximizer lies strictly in the atomic regime: exactly 10% of points favor winding twice. The classification is valid for every width, with explicit limiting behavior at very narrow or broad strips, and compares intrinsically meaningful moduli rather than arbitrary sampled parameter slices.
